family_title_en: Segment and read words with prefixes or suffixes

stages.ix_title: Segment and read words with prefixes or suffixes

prompt.en: Read it. Which is the base word?

stages.choice_rule: Build four different whole-word choices. Exactly one is the base word left after the prefix or suffix is removed. The other three are real words from the roots list or allowed_extra_words and are not the base. Vary answer_index across 0, 1, 2, and 3. If the base spelling changed, set explain_key to drop_e, double_letter, or y_to_i. Otherwise set explain_key to the affix: suffix_ing, suffix_ed, suffix_ly, suffix_er, suffix_s, suffix_y, suffix_est, suffix_ful, suffix_less, prefix_un, prefix_re, prefix_pre, prefix_dis, or prefix_mis.

roots: The stem is exactly one word, and that word has one clear prefix or suffix.
The correct choice is the base word after the affix is removed.
If the spelling changed, undo the change: drop the extra doubled letter, put a silent e back, or turn i back into y.
Wrong choices are real whole words from the roots list or allowed_extra_words.
A wrong choice must not be a second true base of the same stem.
Use only these affixes: un, re, pre, dis, mis, ing, ed, s, es, er, est, ly, y, ful, less.
Do not split compounds or opaque words such as birthday, playground, repeat, remember, or early.
Tier 2 and tier 3 may use the whole affixed word as one wrong choice.
Keep the topic in school, home, food, pets, play, family, or weather, with no brand names.
About one third of the pool is prefixes and about two thirds is suffixes.

tier_rules.1: A short base plus ing, ed, or ly with no spelling change. Wrong choices are other short words that do not sit inside the stem and are not the whole word.
tier_rules.2: A doubled consonant, a dropped silent e, or the suffix er. One wrong choice is a close word, a hidden chunk, or the whole word. The correct base is still easy to see at one end.
tier_rules.3: A prefix un, re, pre, dis, or mis, or a y-to-i change before er, est, or ed. One wrong choice is the whole word with the affix still on. Another is only a letter or two off the true base.

double_letter.en: The base doubled its last letter before the suffix. Drop that extra letter.

y_to_i.en: A final y on the base changed to i before the suffix. Change i back to y.
